cards.text: Job, a man of Uz who has lost his children, his wealth and his health (Job 1:1, 13-19; 2:7), is still talking with his friends. His friend Eliphaz the Temanite just told him his wickedness is great (Job 22:5). Now Job answers: "Even today my complaint is bitter." God's hand is still heavy on him, despite his groaning.

cards.question: Job is hurting, and he has one big wish. What does Job wish he knew?

answers.text: How long his pain will last

cards.text: If Job could find God's seat, he'd go right up, plead his case and fill his mouth with arguments. Friend, I rehearsed a speech EVERY time that junk drawer opened, and nobody ever stuck around to hear it.

cards.question: Job only wants to talk at God. He doesn't care what God would say back.

cards.text: Then Job asks himself a question. If he got there, would God contend with him in His great power?

cards.question: Job answers his own question. What does Job say God would certainly do?
If Job could reason with God, he says he would be delivered forever from his ___.

cards.text: Job goes looking east, west, north and south, and he can't find God anywhere. Friend, four directions is all there IS, and Job checked every single one.

cards.question: Job can't see God anywhere. But Job is sure God knows something. What does God know?
Job says that when God has tested him, he will come forth as ___.

cards.text: Job keeps going. His feet have followed in God's tracks, and he's kept His way without turning aside.

cards.question: Job says he hasn't departed from God's commands. He has treasured the words of God's mouth more than what?

cards.text: Then Job's tone shifts. God is unchangeable, nobody can oppose Him, He does what He desires, and He carries out His decree against Job.

cards.question: Job says this decree against him is the only plan God has for him.
When Job considers all this, he says he is ___ in God's presence.

cards.text: God has made Job's heart faint. And thick darkness covers his face.

cards.question: With thick darkness covering his face, Job says the darkness has silenced him.

cards.text: NOT silenced. Friend, the dark of a junk drawer shut me up for YEARS, and Job is still out here talking.
Now Job asks a big question. Why doesn't the Almighty reserve times for judgment, and why do those who know Him never see His days?

cards.question: Job starts listing wrongs that men do. What's first on his list?

cards.text: And the weakest get hit the hardest. Men drive away the donkey of the fatherless, take the widow's ox in pledge and push the needy off the road.

cards.question: Job says the poor of the land are forced into hiding.

cards.text: The poor forage for food like wild donkeys in the desert and glean the vineyards of the wicked. At night they have no clothing and no covering against the cold.

cards.question: The mountain rains come down, and the poor have no shelter. Where do they huddle?

cards.text: It gets worse. The fatherless infant is snatched from the breast, and the nursing child of the poor is seized for a debt.

cards.question: The poor carry the sheaves, crush the olives and tread the winepresses. What do they get for all that work?

answers.text: They still go hungry and thirsty

cards.question: Men groan from the city, and the wounded cry out. Yet Job says God charges ___ with wrongdoing.

cards.text: Then Job turns to another crowd: those who rebel against the light. They don't know its ways, and they don't stay on its paths.

cards.question: These people rebel against the light. So when does the murderer rise to kill the poor and needy?

cards.text: The adulterer watches for twilight, thinks no eye will see him, and covers his face. Friend, my mustache covers HALF my face, and everybody still knows exactly who I am.

cards.question: By day, these people who dig through houses in the dark come out into the light like everyone else.

cards.text: For them, deep darkness is their morning. Friend, I spent years in a dark drawer, and I would have given ANYTHING for a real morning.

cards.question: Job says these people are but foam on the surface of the water. What is that picture saying about them?
Job says Sheol steals those who have sinned. What does he compare that to?
Job says these sinners will be remembered for generations.

cards.text: So injustice is broken like a tree. These are the ones who prey on the barren and childless and show no kindness to the widow.
Yet by His power, God drags away the mighty. Even when they rise up, they have no assurance of life.

cards.question: God gives the mighty a sense of security. But what does Job say is really going on?

answers.text: His eyes are on their ways

cards.question: Job says the mighty are exalted for a ___, and then they are gone.

cards.text: They're brought low and gathered up like all others. They're cut off like heads of grain.

cards.question: Job ends with a challenge. If what he's said isn't so, what does he dare anyone to do?

cards.text: That's Job's case, and he just dared the whole room. Trust me, friend, this story is still in the oven.

findings.problem: The opening card has 4 sentences: Job's introduction, Eliphaz's charge, Job's answer, and the heavy hand. That is over the limit.

rule.text: The opening card can be up to 3 sentences. It says who is speaking, to whom, and what is going on.

findings.problem: The right answer "Judge" is capitalized, as in the BSB, and the wrong answers "friends" and "enemies" are lowercase. The capital letter points to the right answer.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike. None should sound more like the Bible, or more modern, than the others.

findings.problem: The blank asks the baker to finish Job's line with a surprising word ("Judge"). Nothing on the earlier cards lets the baker reason it out, so this tests wording the baker hasn't seen, not meaning.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: Job 23:8-9 is conditional ("If I go east... if I go west"). The card turns it into something Job actually did: "Job goes looking east, west, north and south" and "Job checked every single one."
This story card only repeats the answer to card 17 ("NOT silenced") and adds a joke. It cites Job 23:17 again and tells nothing new, so it doesn't move the passage forward.

rule.text: Every story card moves the baker forward through the passage.

findings.problem: This is a where question. The wrong answer "In a borrowed tent" is not a real detail from the Bible.

rule.text: For who, which thing and where questions, wrong answers are real details from somewhere in the Bible, like Joppa when the right answer is Tarshish.

findings.problem: The right answer, "They still go hungry and thirsty," is a full clause and longer than the others. The wrong answers, "A share of the harvest" and "A house in the city," are short noun phrases. The difference in form and length makes the right answer stand out.

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone. None are silly.

findings.problem: The right answer, "His eyes are on their ways," uses biblical phrasing. The wrong answers, "He has stopped watching them" and "He has forgotten their names," are plain modern wording. The tone gives the right answer away.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike. None should sound more like the Bible, or more modern, than the others.
